_comment: Provenance for the CPython iOS payload. scripts/fetch_python_ios.sh is the only thing that reads this, and third_party/python-ios/ is untracked: the artifact is an immutable upstream release, so it is fetched rather than committed. IOS-POC-7E.

upstream.hash_evidence: Downloaded 2026-09-18 and again 2026-09-21; both copies hash to the value above, so the release asset is immutable and re-fetching reproduces it byte for byte.

contents.note: No macOS slice. `swift test` runs on macOS and therefore cannot execute this interpreter; anything that needs CPython has to run in the Simulator.

licences._note: Recorded from the upstream project's own documentation as a starting point. This is not an independent licence audit; one belongs to whatever stage first ships a build to anyone other than the author.

trim_note: Only obvious non-shippables. `test` alone is 35 MB of the 50 MB shared standard library. lib-dynload is deliberately NOT trimmed: dropping a .so there turns into an ImportError at runtime in whichever script happens to need it, and the payload is untracked anyway, so the disk it costs is cheap. Revisit when app size is the thing being measured.

python_packages._comment: Pure-Python wheels vendored so a spider's `import requests` resolves. IOS-POC-7P. Every one is py3-none-any: nothing here compiles, and the interpreter already carries the C extensions they need (_ssl, _socket, _hashlib, select). Unpacked into third_party/python-ios/site-packages, which is untracked like the rest.
python_packages.why: Measured at IOS-POC-7L: `requests` is the only thing blocking 13 of the 42 configured Python sites, and `urllib3` blocks one more on its own — which this covers for free, since urllib3 is requests' own dependency.

licences._note: From each project's own metadata; not an independent audit.

python_packages._comment_ios_poc_37: IOS-POC-37 appended bs4 (+ soupsieve, typing-extensions: its declared runtime requirements) and pyquery (+ cssselect). All py3-none-any. pyquery also needs lxml, which is native and lives in python_native_packages.

python_native_packages._comment: IOS-POC-37. Packages with C code, cross-compiled here from pinned upstream sources by scripts/build_python_ios_native.sh with the official cross-venv tooling Python-Apple-support ships in each slice (platform-config/*/make_cross_venv.py). Nothing here is a downloaded binary: PyPI has no iOS wheel for pycryptodome or lxml, and pycryptodome's maintainer calls iOS unsupported (Legrandin/pycryptodome#907, #584). Output goes to third_party/python-ios/native/<sdk>/, untracked like the rest; the Install Python build phase copies the right sdk's tree into the bundle and turns every .so into a framework.
python_native_packages.targets_note: arm64 only for the Simulator: the Install Python phase copies lib-$ARCHS, so a Simulator build is single-arch anyway, and every Mac this project builds on is Apple silicon. An x86_64 Simulator build would find no native tree and fail at import, not silently.

sources.note: Same libxml2 2.14.6 / libxslt 1.1.43 its official 6.1.3 wheels are built with (.github/workflows/wheels.yml at tag lxml-6.1.3). zlib and iconv come from the iOS SDK rather than being built, and lxml.objectify is left out (WITHOUT_OBJECTIFY): no configured spider uses it.
